name: rust-sitter
description: Write tree-sitter grammars as annotated Rust types via a macro

license.comment: `license = "MIT"` in runtime/Cargo.toml; crates.io and the GitHub licence badge agree. The companion `rust-sitter-macro` and `rust-sitter-tool` crates are MIT as well.

approach.comment: Per the RESEARCH.md Assessment Guideline (`rust-sitter` = `generator-macro` + `incremental-cst`). Grammar is expressed as `#[rust_sitter::grammar]` / `#[leaf]` / `#[prec_left]` attributes on Rust types; the tool extracts a tree-sitter grammar from them and generates the parser. The incremental CST engine is tree-sitter's, but the public API only exposes a typed AST (see Incremental Reparsing).

implementation.comment: Wraps the tree-sitter engine. Default feature `tree-sitter-c2rust` uses a c2rust-transpiled Rust copy of the runtime ("1:1 correspondence with the original C code"); `tree-sitter-standard` swaps in the C runtime. Either way the grammar itself is emitted as C (`parser.c`) by `tree-sitter-generate` and compiled with `cc` in `build.rs`, so a C compiler is always in the build and the dependency tree is not C-free.

crates-io.comment: Runtime crate. Companions: `rust-sitter-macro` (proc-macros), `rust-sitter-tool` (build-dependency that extracts the grammar and compiles the parser), `rust-sitter-common`.

documentation.comment: No dedicated book; the README is the long-form guide and docs.rs documents each attribute macro (docs.rs reports ~59% item coverage).

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; 0.4.5 published 2025-05-06 and bundles tree-sitter 0.25.2. Research reflects 0.4.5 / `main` (last commit 2025-06-18).

grammar-class.comment: The tool hands the extracted grammar to `tree_sitter_generate::generate_parser_for_grammar`, so the accepted class is tree-sitter's: GLR over LR(1) tables. Inherited, not re-implemented.

grammar-definition.comment: Grammar lives in a Rust module annotated `#[rust_sitter::grammar("name")]`, with `#[language]`, `#[leaf(pattern|text, transform)]`, `#[prec]`/`#[prec_left]`/`#[prec_right]`, `#[extra]`, `#[repeat]`, `#[delimited]`, `#[skip]`, `#[word]` attributes on structs/enums/fields. No external grammar file is written by the user; `build.rs` re-parses the source with `syn` to extract it.

left-recursion.comment: LR/GLR tables from tree-sitter; the README/example arithmetic grammar defines `Sub(Box<Expr>, '-', Box<Expr>)` as a left-recursive `#[prec_left(1)]` variant. LR generators get `native` per the guideline.

ambiguity-handling.comment: Unresolved LR(1) conflicts make `tree_sitter_generate` fail inside `build.rs`; the user resolves them with `#[prec]`/`#[prec_left]`/`#[prec_right]`. The attribute set exposes no equivalent of tree-sitter's `conflicts` list, so the GLR `all-parses` path is not reachable from rust-sitter's DSL.

backtracking.comment: Deterministic table-driven tree-sitter parser; no backtracking or cut operators in the DSL.

lexer-integration.comment: Tokens are declared inline with `#[leaf(text = "...")]` / `#[leaf(pattern = r"...")]` and lexed by the generated tree-sitter parser; no external token stream can be supplied. Tree-sitter external scanners (C) are not exposed.

precedence-pratt-support.comment: `#[rust_sitter::prec(n)]`, `#[prec_left(n)]`, `#[prec_right(n)]` map to tree-sitter's `prec`/`prec.left`/`prec.right`; the README example uses them for `-` vs `*`.

unicode-aware.comment: Input is `&str` (UTF-8 enforced by the type), `#[leaf]` patterns are tree-sitter regexes matched on code points, and `transform` closures receive the token as `&str`. Spans are byte offsets, not char indices.

input-types.comment: Generated entry point is `pub fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<Root, Vec<ParseError>>`; it calls `tree_sitter::Parser::parse(input, None)` internally. The rope/callback inputs of the underlying tree-sitter API are not surfaced.

streaming-partial-input.comment: `parse` consumes a complete `&str` and returns either the AST or errors; there is no "need more input" signal.

zero-copy.comment: The generated `parse(input: &str) -> Result<Root, _>` has no lifetime tying `Root` to `input`, and `Extract`/`WithLeaf` use `dyn Fn(&str) -> L` transforms that must produce owned values; leaf text is typically copied into `String`/parsed numbers. The tree-sitter tree is dropped after extraction.

span-tracking.comment: Opt-in per field/type via `Spanned<T> { value: T, span: (usize, usize) }` — byte start (inclusive) / end (exclusive) into the source. No line/column; `ParseError` carries the same `start`/`end` byte offsets.

output-model.comment: The annotated Rust structs/enums *are* the AST; `Extract` impls for `Box`, `Vec`, `Option`, `Spanned`, `WithLeaf` walk the tree-sitter tree and build them. The generic tree-sitter CST is internal and not returned.

semantic-actions.comment: Actions are limited to leaf `transform = |text: &str| ...` closures (e.g. `v.parse().unwrap()`) and the structural mapping implied by the field types; there are no per-rule action blocks for non-terminals, and the `Extract` trait can be implemented by hand for custom types.

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: `#[rust_sitter::extra]` on a struct (typically `#[leaf(pattern = r"\s")]`) maps to tree-sitter `extras`; such nodes "can safely be skipped while parsing" and do not appear in the typed AST.

stateful-parsing.comment: `parse(input)` takes no user state and the `Extract` trait passes only node, source bytes, last index and an optional leaf closure; no state threading facility exists.

error-recovery.comment: Inherits tree-sitter's built-in, non-configurable repair (`ERROR`/`MISSING` nodes), which `collect_parsing_errors` converts into `ParseError { reason: UnexpectedToken | MissingToken | FailedNode(Vec<ParseError>), start, end }`. Caveat: if `root_node.has_error()` the whole parse returns `Err(errors)` — no partial typed AST is produced, so recovery only serves diagnostics, not partial results.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: `Err(Vec<ParseError>)`; `collect_parsing_errors` "accumulates all errors that were emitted" across the tree, nesting them as `FailedNode` for `ERROR` nodes with children.

expected-token-reporting.comment: `UnexpectedToken(String)` carries the offending text and `MissingToken(String)` names the single token tree-sitter inserted; neither carries the set of tokens that would have been valid.

custom-error-types.comment: Return type is fixed to `Vec<::rust_sitter::errors::ParseError>` by the generated code; no generic error parameter.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Every `ParseError` has byte-range `start`/`end` (4 per guideline); nested `FailedNode` errors give a crude hierarchy but there are no labels or secondary spans, and no line/column.

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: No ariadne/miette/codespan-reporting/annotate-snippets dependency or documented bridge; the README only says `Spanned` is "useful for diagnostic tools".

contextual-error-messages.comment: None of the attribute macros attach labels or expectations to rules; errors carry only reason and span.

incremental-reparsing.comment: The generated `parse` creates a fresh `Parser`, calls `parser.parse(input, None)` (no old tree) and discards the tree after extraction. The `rust_sitter::tree_sitter` re-export plus the generated `language()` function would let a user drive tree-sitter's `Tree::edit` path themselves, but rust-sitter's own API does not expose it.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Output is the user's typed AST; `#[extra]` whitespace/comment nodes are skipped and punctuation leaves are dropped unless the user keeps them as fields. The underlying tree-sitter CST is not returned.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No queries are generated and the tree never leaves `parse`; the `tree_sitter::Query` API is technically reachable via the re-export and `language()` but is undocumented for rust-sitter grammars.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: crates.io reverse dependencies (5 crates, checked 2026-09-19) contain no editor or language server.

runtime-speed-tier.comment: No independent benchmark of rust-sitter found. Underlying engine is tree-sitter (default via c2rust-transpiled runtime, whose relative speed is unmeasured) plus a post-parse extraction walk; left `null` per guideline.

compile-time-impact.comment: No published measurement. Expect non-trivial cost: `build.rs` pulls `syn` (full), `tree-sitter-generate` and `cc`, re-parses the source to extract the grammar, runs table generation and compiles `parser.c` on every change to the grammar module. Left `null` per guideline.

allocation-strategy.comment: Tree-sitter heap-allocates its subtree nodes, then extraction builds the typed AST with `Box`/`Vec`/`String` per node; no arena or allocator hook.

generated-code-size.comment: Generates a tree-sitter `parser.c` (LR/GLR tables) per grammar and compiles it with `cc`; tree-sitter tables are routinely multi-megabyte for real languages (issue #1041: 8.7 MB TypeScript, 25 MB Zig). Small DSLs produce proportionally smaller files.

no-std-support.comment: No `no_std` attribute or `std` feature; runtime uses `std::` paths and `Vec`/`String`, and the parser depends on the tree-sitter runtime plus a C-compiled grammar.

msrv.comment: No `rust-version` in any Cargo.toml, no README statement, and CI tests stable only. Edition 2021.

unsafe-usage.comment: The runtime crate's own code has no `unsafe`, but the generated code declares `extern "C" { fn tree_sitter_<name>() -> Language; }` and calls it in `unsafe {}` to link the C-compiled grammar; the default `tree-sitter-c2rust` runtime is machine-transpiled C and correspondingly unsafe-heavy. No `forbid(unsafe_code)`.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: `rust-sitter-macro` (`proc-macro = true`) is a non-optional dependency; the entire grammar DSL is attribute macros.

build-rs-step.comment: Required: `build.rs` must call `rust_sitter_tool::build_parsers(&PathBuf::from("src/main.rs"))`, which extracts the grammar with `syn`, runs `tree-sitter-generate`, and compiles `parser.c` with `cc` (C11).

dependency-count.comment: Runtime crate with default features: `rust-sitter-macro` + `tree-sitter-c2rust` (0.25.2). `tree-sitter` (C runtime) is the optional alternative behind `tree-sitter-standard`. Build-time `rust-sitter-tool` additionally pulls `syn`, `syn-inline-mod`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `tree-sitter`, `tree-sitter-generate`, `cc`, `tempfile`. Checked at 0.4.5.

wasm-compatible.comment: Stated design goal ("pure-Rust runtime to support `wasm32-unknown-unknown`"); CI runs `cargo test -p rust-sitter-example --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. The tool writes a stub sysroot (`stdint.h`, `stdlib.h`, ...) so `cc` can compile `parser.c` for wasm32, so a wasm-capable C compiler (clang) is still needed.

async-friendly.comment: `parse` is a plain synchronous function returning an owned AST of user-defined types (no tree-sitter handles retained), so results are `Send` whenever the user's types are. Input must be fully materialised as `&str` first.

maintenance-status.comment: Last commit 2025-06-18 and last release 2025-05-06 — more than 12 months before 2026-09-19, so not `actively-maintained`. Recent history is tree-sitter version bumps and small fixes from outside contributors merged by the author; repo not archived. Time-sensitive.

documentation-quality.comment: Thorough README walkthrough (installation, every attribute, `Spanned`, `Vec`/`Option`/`Box`, debugging artifacts) and per-macro docs.rs pages with examples; but no book, no cookbook, no migration notes, and docs.rs coverage ~59% (e.g. `ParseErrorReason` variants undocumented). 3 per guideline.

tutorial-book.comment: README-only; no dedicated long-form guide or site.

notable-users.value: Hydro project (dfir_datalog_core, formerly hydroflow_datalog_core — the Datalog frontend), tree-sitter-sleigh
notable-users.comment: Only five crates.io reverse dependencies as of 2026-09-19, most of them from the author's own Hydro project (which rust-sitter was built for). No widely known external adopter verified.

bus-factor.comment: Shadaj Laddad authored 89 of ~106 commits and is the sole listed crate author; all other contributors have 1–3 commits. Hosted under the `hydro-project` GitHub organisation (UC Berkeley Hydro research group), which mitigates but does not change the single-maintainer reality.
